intro: Brief is where your team writes together. Every document is a rich-text page you can co-edit live, comment on in the margins, version, and organize into folders scoped to a project. This chapter takes you from a blank page to a published document, shows how two people type at once without stepping on each other, and points out where an AI agent can do the things the buttons cannot. By the end you will be able to write, format, publish, and promote a document, and find any of them fast.
atAGlance: Rich-text editing on Tiptap, with a formatting toolbar and slash commands
Real-time co-editing with live cursors and presence, merged conflict-free
Four-status lifecycle: Draft, In Review, Approved, and Archived
Folders, project scope, versions, comments, and stars to keep work tidy
Promote a finished document one-way into a Beacon knowledge-base article

quiz.q: What are Brief's four document statuses?
choices: Draft, In Review, Approved, and Archived
Open, In Progress, Closed, and Archived
quiz.answer: Draft, In Review, Approved, and Archived

quiz.q: Which visibility level does the menu list but reject as invalid?
What status does a document have after you click Publish, and what status after Save Draft?
quiz.answer: Publish sets the document to Approved; Save Draft keeps it as Draft.

quiz.q: How long can a document icon be?
What are the three valid visibility levels and who can see a document at each?
quiz.answer: Organization (all org members), Project (the creator, collaborators, or members of that project), and Private (the creator and collaborators only).

quiz.q: How many MCP tools does Brief expose to agents?
What technology does Brief use to merge concurrent edits without overwriting, and over what connection?
quiz.answer: A conflict-free shared editing model (Yjs) over the /brief/ws WebSocket.
quiz.where: Edit an existing document and co-edit in real time

quiz.q: What happens when you promote a document to Beacon?
choices: Brief creates a Beacon article from it, and the promotion is one-way
The document is deleted after the article is created
It can be promoted again to refresh the article
A draft copy is made and nothing is sent to Beacon
quiz.answer: Brief creates a Beacon article from it, and the promotion is one-way

quiz.q: Which folder actions can the Brief UI do, and which require an agent or the API?
quiz.answer: The UI can only create folders; renaming, moving, and deleting folders are done through an agent or the API.

quiz.q: How many characters must you type before Search returns results?
Why should you avoid the "Brief summary (optional)" field, and what should you do instead?
quiz.answer: It is not stored by Brief today, so anything typed there is dropped on save; put summary text in the document body instead.

quiz.q: What does the Duplicate action create?
choices: An Approved copy with the same title
A new version on the same document
A Beacon article from the document
